Only what the chart states is recorded; nothing is deduced. Services, frequencies, elevation, position, magnetic variation and runways
were first extracted automatically from the chart text; the reporting points, rules and notes were added by hand.
The charts themselves are (c) SIA and are not redistributed. Flight simulation only: never use for real navigation.
No circuit height or circuit side is printed on this chart, so none is recorded. The radials and distances from BNE drawn beside the reporting points are not recorded.

radio.arrival: on arrival and in transit, radio contact with Le Touquet TWR is recommended at least 5 minutes before entering the CTR

notes: Preferred runway 13, due to the IFR procedure.
The aerodrome can be covered by sea haze within a few minutes.
Heavy VFR activity on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.
VFR flights may be given special VFR routes and reporting points by ATC.
Special VFR meteorological minima in the CTR when IFR traffic is present: ceiling 800 ft QNH for aeroplanes, 600 ft QNH for helicopters; visibility 2000 m.
Southern departures: avoid overflying Berck-sur-Mer aerodrome (LFAM).
Avoid overflying the private aerodrome Le Portel Alprech, whose traffic pattern is at 700 ft AMSL.
Take-off runway 31: when passing the runway end, and not before 300 ft ASFC, turn 10 degrees right to avoid the built-up areas; do not turn left before 1000 ft ASFC.
Crosswind limits on runway 13/31: 20 kt on a wet runway, 25 kt on a dry runway.
TORA, TODA, ASDA and LDA of runway 13 are reduced because of the localizer shelter.
Hot spot: holding point P1 is far from the runway, on the taxiway parallel to the runway; risk of runway incursion if it is not observed.
Night VFR is approved; on runway 31 the PAPI is compulsory.

Outside ATS hours the runway 31 pilot-controlled lighting and PAPI are set on the air-air frequency: 3 clicks on the microphone for low intensity, 5 for high intensity, 7 within 5 seconds to switch off; automatic shut-off after 15 minutes.
Radio failure: air traffic light signals and pyrotechnic signals are unserviceable.
